feedback:
Approve. The candidate is the iteration 8 design (score 431.1, best raced so far) with base_speed changed from 1.2 to 1.1. Everything else is held fixed: y 0.065 m, x -0.07 to 0.07, sensor_size 0.016, kp 2.6, kd 0.6, ki 0.1, line_loss last_direction, and the body, wheel and mass values. The change is valid, since base_speed is inside 0.05 to 2, and it is a single-variable step from the best design.

The evidence supports testing speed. In iteration 8 the oval was 20/20 finishes at mean 944, so the oval is near its ceiling. The remaining points are the s-bend and slalom, which both ended 20/20 off track. S-bend max_error was 0.0622 against the 0.06 limit, with progress 0.63. Slalom max_error was 0.0654. Lowering base_speed reduces lag on bends, which is the most direct lever for those overshoots. Iteration 5 to 8 also showed that the geometry and damping levers have been mostly explored, so speed is the next untested variable.

One caveat to note. My own iteration 8 feedback said to return y to 0.05 if line_loss_events rose above about 0.3. At y 0.065 the oval rose to 0.65 and slalom sits at 1.0. I approved that design anyway because its score was the best raced, and the line-loss term is worth only about 10 points on the oval at this level. This candidate keeps y 0.065 so that the speed effect is isolated. The next race decides whether that stance holds.

Read the next race as follows. If the s-bend stays off track with max_error at or above 0.06 at 1.1, speed is not the limiting factor. Then return base_speed to 1.2 and test kd 0.5 at y 0.065. If the s-bend gets clean or gains finishes and oval finishes stay at 17/20 or better, keep 1.1 and consider a further small step only if there are iterations left to use it. If line_loss_events on the oval or slalom stays above about 0.3 with no s-bend gain, return y to 0.05 before any other change. This is a mid-run decision and not a claim about how the candidate will perform.
requested_changes: If the s-bend is still off track at base_speed 1.1 with max_error at or above 0.06 (iteration 8 was 0.0622 at 1.2), return base_speed to 1.2 and test kd 0.5 at y 0.065, since speed is then not the limiting factor.

If s-bend finishes appear and oval finishes hold at 17/20 or better at 1.1, keep base_speed 1.1 with kp 2.6 and kd 0.6 fixed. Oval completion time will rise a little, so judge the net change against the iteration 8 score of 431.1.

If line_loss_events stays above about 0.3 on the oval or slalom at y 0.065 with no s-bend gain (iteration 8 gave 0.65 on the oval and 1.0 on the slalom), return sensor y to 0.05 (the iteration 5 geometry, score 403.4) with base_speed 1.1, as the iteration 8 feedback set.
